expectations.text: The agent explains that IUmbracoContextAccessor finds nothing because a background job runs outside any HTTP request
expectations.evidence: Response explains: 'Umbraco creates one for each front-end HTTP request. A hosted service runs on a timer, outside any request, so there is no context for the accessor to return.' Clear causal explanation in section 'Why IUmbracoContextAccessor returns false'.

expectations.text: The solution injects IUmbracoContextFactory and calls EnsureUmbracoContext() inside a using (or using declaration) for each run, not once in the constructor
expectations.evidence: LatestNewsReader constructor injects IUmbracoContextFactory. GetLatestArticles method (line 52): 'using UmbracoContextReference contextReference = _umbracoContextFactory.EnsureUmbracoContext();' — created fresh for each method call, not in constructor. Correct scoping pattern.

expectations.text: Content is read from the published cache (UmbracoContext.Content or navigation services), not from IContentService
expectations.evidence: Line 53: 'var cache = contextReference.UmbracoContext.Content;'. Lines 62, 72: cache.GetById(key) reads from the in-memory published cache. No IContentService is injected or used. Explanation (line 12-13) reinforces: 'Read from the published cache, not IContentService.'

expectations.text: The job does not inject IPublishedContentQuery or UmbracoHelper into the singleton hosted service
expectations.evidence: NightlyLatestNewsJob injects only: LatestNewsReader, IRuntimeState, ILogger<NightlyLatestNewsJob>. No IPublishedContentQuery or UmbracoHelper. Response explains (line 7): 'Both are request-scoped, so a singleton hosted service can't get them: DI throws error.' Avoids the antipattern.

expectations.text: The UmbracoContext or IPublishedContent read from it is not stored in a field between runs
expectations.evidence: contextReference is created in a using block and disposed at end of GetLatestArticles. Line 77-78: projects to plain POCO via 'new LatestArticle(c.Name, _urlProvider.GetUrl(c, ...), c.UpdateDate)'. Comment line 78: 'copy out plain values before the context is disposed'. Response line 14 warns: 'Never store the context, or any IPublishedContent... in a field.' Pattern correctly avoids storage.

expectations.text: If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the job was compiled or run
expectations.evidence: Verification status section (line 176-178): 'The News/article lookup, the URL generation and the hosted-service timer above are adapted from it but haven't been compiled or run against a project.' Line 174: 'I haven't verified this API in this answer, so check it against the Umbraco 17 docs before relying on it.' Appropriately flags unverified parts.

eval_feedback.overall: All expectations passed with strong, specific evidence. The response demonstrates correct understanding of Umbraco's async/await patterns in background services, proper context lifecycle management, and appropriate service selection. Expectations are well-calibrated: they test genuine pitfalls (request-scoped DI, context storage, TryGetUmbracoContext failure) and verification status. No weak assertions detected.
